meaning: One job behind the arm with one part of the machine that it exhausts first; the dive counts fifteen.
A piece of a computer that fills separately from the others, such as CPU cores, memory bandwidth or a GPU's tensor cores.
The part of the machine a job exhausts first: the resource that is full while the rest of the machine sits partly idle.
Three properties of a job: how long one unit runs, whether its pieces exchange data while running, and whether it can lose its machine and resume.
How long one unit of a job's work runs.
Whether a job's pieces must exchange data while they run.
Whether a job can lose its machine and resume having lost no more than one unit.
The trained model that reads the cameras and joint angles and decides what the motors do next.
The rate at which memory delivers data to the processor.
One attempt at the task, recorded or simulated: a table of joint readings and motor commands over time, plus video from each camera.
The open-source robot-learning library whose defaults the arm follows.
The video compression format LeRobot writes by default, encoded and decoded by CPU code.
A model that predicts what happens next, given what the robot sees and an action it might take.
The GPU's units for matrix arithmetic, used by training and inference.
Separate GPU units that follow light rays to draw an image.
Fixed circuits on a GPU that only compress and decompress video.
The copy of a model saved to storage during a training run, from which a stopped run resumes.
One AWS Batch submission that spawns many child jobs, each reading its own index.
EC2 capacity that AWS can take back after a notice issued two minutes before, on a best-effort basis.
A program of six 1024x1024 float32 matrices, each multiplying a vector in turn, run on one CPU core: small enough to count by hand, and not the arm's policy.
One of the eight steps an episode passes through in the loop; one stage can hold several workloads.
NVIDIA's inference compiler; the fastest runtime in its benchmark table for the Jetson Orin.
NVIDIA's ray-tracing renderer, which needs a GPU with RT cores.
The way capacity is bought: on demand, reserved ahead, or as spare capacity that can be taken back.
A job shape: short pieces that need nothing from each other; a lost machine costs the unit it was running.
A job shape: machines that exchange data at every step; losing one loses the step on all.
The run of future actions one policy call returns (40 in NVIDIA's GR00T N1.7 benchmark); the arm plays them while the next call computes.
The units of a GPU that run any arithmetic in parallel, as distinct from its tensor cores, ray-tracing cores and video engines.
A job shape: one machine for hours; a stop costs the work since the last checkpoint.
A job shape: a stream with no end, handled item by item on machines kept running; a taken machine costs one item.
A job shape: work on the computer beside the arm that cannot be interrupted and has no cloud scheduler.
Software on a device that receives deployments from the cloud; it delivers the model to the computer beside the arm.
Multiplying a recorded episode into variants to get more training samples.
